rows.title: Monetary Policy
rows.figure: Fed Dec hike ~85% 25bp / ~14.5% 50bp (CME FedWatch); ECB Dec ~88%; BoJ Dec ~84%; BoE Dec ~70–75%; BoC Dec ~32–36%; US 2Y ~4.86% (+34bp in two sessions)
rows.read: New York Fed President John Williams, the Fed's number two, said the Fed still has work to do, backing a December hike and more after it. Europe, Britain and Japan are also expected to hike, but US rates are rising faster, so the gap keeps favouring the dollar.

rows.title: Growth
rows.figure: UK Q3 GDP +0.7% q/q (in line); US jobless claims 200K; euro-area Q3 GDP 2nd est. today 4:00 AM CT, fcst +0.4% q/q
rows.read: The US economy still looks firmer than Australia, Canada or New Zealand, which keeps the dollar ahead of those currencies. Euro-area growth figures this morning show whether Europe is keeping up.

rows.title: Inflation
rows.figure: US Oct CPI +0.4% m/m; US PPI today 7:30 AM CT fcst +0.4% m/m (core +0.3%); Japan Oct wholesale prices +7.1% y/y; Brent ~$96.5
rows.read: US inflation is running at about twice the Fed's goal, and oil's climb back toward $97 adds to that worry. That keeps the Fed hiking and supports the dollar. US producer prices this morning are the next check.

rows.title: Risk Sentiment
rows.figure: Bitcoin −4% to ~$68,600, lowest since August (Reuters); AUD/USD ~0.681, NZD/USD ~0.555; USD/CHF ~0.835
rows.read: Tech shares and Bitcoin are sliding, but not enough to send money into safe havens, so the franc and yen get no lift. The Aussie and kiwi, which track the market mood, stay near their lows.

rows.title: Terms of Trade
rows.figure: Brent ~$96.5, WTI ~$88.9 (~1:00 AM CT); Thu settle Brent $95.82 (+$3.06); gold ~$3,875
rows.read: Oil climbed back after attacks on Saudi energy sites, while gold sits at its lowest in more than a year. Dearer oil helps the Canadian dollar and hurts energy buyers like Japan and the euro area. Weak gold takes some support from the Aussie.

rows.title: Positioning
rows.figure: CFTC Nov 3: hedge funds for USD, JPY, AUD, GBP; against NZD, CAD, EUR; 4-week change NZD −22K, EUR −34K contracts; next report Friday
rows.read: Hedge funds lean toward the dollar and against the kiwi, the Canadian dollar and the euro, and this week's moves went their way. Their large bet on the yen keeps losing money as it weakens. A fresh weekly report from US regulators is due today.

rows.title: Fiscal
rows.figure: October deficit $404B, a record for the month; US 10-year ~5.11%; 30-year auction 5.441%, bid-to-cover 2.36
rows.read: Record US government borrowing and soft demand at this week's bond sales keep long-term US borrowing costs above 5%. Higher yields support the dollar for now, but a growing deficit is a worry if buyers start asking for more.
